questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of prosopagnosia?

options.text: It is the inability to recognize faces
The recognition of other environmental objects is also usually impaired
It is thought to result from disconnection of the left inferior temporal cortex from the left frontal lobe
It is the same as associative visual agnosia
It usually occurs early on in frontotemporal dementia

correct_answer.text: It is the inability to recognize faces

correct_answers.text: It is the inability to recognize faces

questions.explanation: Prosopagnosia is a neuropsychological condition in which the patient is unable to recognize faces. 'The man who mistook his wife for a hat' is a well-known clinical story exemplifying this condition. The recognition of other environmental objects is preserved. There are radiological and pathological findings indicating the association of disconnection of the left inferior temporal cortex from the visual association area in the left parietal lobe leading to prosopagnosia. In a similar condition, associative visual agnosia results from bilateral medial occipitotemporal lesions, where the patient is also unable to name the objects but the ability to draw them is preserved. Both conditions occur in advanced Alzheimer's disease and with vascular pathology.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about disorders of visual perception, except:

options.text: Apperceptive visual agnosia results from bilateral lesions in the visual association areas
Colour perception may be ablated in lesions of the dominant occipital lobe
Colour agnosia is the inability to name a colour despite the ability to point to it
Central achromatopsia is a complete inability to perceive colour
Simultanagnosia is the inability to integrate a visual scene to perceive it as a whole

correct_answer.text: Colour agnosia is the inability to name a colour despite the ability to point to it

correct_answers.text: Colour agnosia is the inability to name a colour despite the ability to point to it

questions.explanation: Apperceptive agnosia patients are unable to identify and draw objects using visual cues. In this condition, other sensory modalities are preserved. It is thought to be a result of impaired transmission of information from the higher visual sensory pathway to visual association areas. Bilateral pathology in visual association areas is associated with the development of apperceptive agnosia. In a similar condition, associative visual agnosia patients are able to draw the item, but are unable to name it, as a result of medial occipital temporal lesions occurring bilaterally.

questions.question_text: Balint's syndrome includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Failure to acknowledge blindness
Optic ataxia
Oculomotor apraxia
Simultanagnosia
Bilateral lesion in the occipitoparietal area

correct_answer.text: Failure to acknowledge blindness

correct_answers.text: Failure to acknowledge blindness

questions.explanation: The triad of Balint's syndrome includes optic ataxia (the inability to direct optically guided movements), oculomotor apraxia (the inability to direct the gaze rapidly) and simultanagnosia. Failure to acknowledge blindness is Anton's syndrome, which is seen with bilateral occipital lesions.

questions.question_text: Gerstmann's syndrome includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Agraphia
Acalculia
Finger agnosia
Right–left disorientation
Dominant temporal lobe lesions

correct_answer.text: Dominant temporal lobe lesions

correct_answers.text: Dominant temporal lobe lesions

questions.explanation: Gerstmann's syndrome has been attributed to dominant parietal lobe lesions.

questions.question_text: Regarding the auditory system, which of the following is true?

options.text: Sound localization is mediated by the dominant hemisphere in the brain
Lexical processing is done in the right temporal lobe
The syndrome of word deafness may reflect damage to the left parietal cortex
The syndrome of auditory sound agnosia is the inability to recognize verbal sounds
All of the above

correct_answer.text: The syndrome of word deafness may reflect damage to the left parietal cortex

correct_answers.text: The syndrome of word deafness may reflect damage to the left parietal cortex

questions.explanation: Sound localization is mediated by the non-dominant hemisphere in the brain. Lexical processing (the extraction of vowels, consonants and words from the auditory input) is done in the higher language association areas in the left temporal lobe. Word deafness is intact hearing for voices but an inability to recognize speech, thought to be due to a disconnection of the auditory cortex from Wernicke's area.

questions.question_text: Which of the following apraxias is correctly paired with its lesion or lesion site?

options.text: Limb-kinetic apraxia–Supplementary motor area
Ideomotor apraxia–Disconnection of Wernicke's area from the motor region
Ideomotor apraxia–Left premotor area
Ideational apraxia–Prefrontal cortex
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: In limb-kinetic apraxia, the patient is unable to use the hand on the opposite side of the lesion (contralateral hand), although the strength of that hand is preserved. In ideomotor apraxia, the patient is not able to perform a motor act when the command is given. However, the patient is able to understand the command and the strength of muscles is preserved. Patients will also be able to perform the same act spontaneously. A lesion in Wernicke's area resulting in impairment in obeying verbal commands and a lesion in the left premotor area resulting in an impairment in the motor programming can cause ideomotor apraxia. In ideational apraxia, the patient is able to perform the individual components of a complex motor task, but unable to perform the entire act as a whole.

questions.question_text: Regarding clinical syndromes of language impairment, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In pure word deafness, the patient can speak fluently and virtually without error and can write normally
In pure word blindness, the patient can describe or copy letters even though he or she cannot recognize them
In pure word dumbness, the patient can repeat the words heard and can read aloud
In pure agraphia, comprehension of written and spoken material is normal and the patient's own speech is unimpaired
In pure word blindness, the patient can write spontaneously and to dictation

correct_answer.text: In pure word dumbness, the patient can repeat the words heard and can read aloud

correct_answers.text: In pure word dumbness, the patient can repeat the words heard and can read aloud

questions.explanation: In pure word deafness (verbal auditory agnosia), the defect is restricted to the understanding of spoken speech. In pure word blindness (alexia without agraphia), the difficulties are entirely restricted to understanding the written word. In pure word dumbness, the patient can comprehend both spoken speech and written material without difficulty; the defect is restricted to the production of spoken speech, which is marked by slurring and dysarthria, and the patient cannot speak at will, repeat words heard or read aloud.

questions.question_text: In Wernicke's dysphasia, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: There is defective appreciation of the meaning of words
Paraphrasic errors and neologisms are frequent
Errors of grammar and syntax occur
Faulty, non-fluent speech is produced with effort
Normal rhythm and inflection are preserved and there are no articulatory defects

correct_answer.text: Faulty, non-fluent speech is produced with effort

correct_answers.text: Faulty, non-fluent speech is produced with effort

questions.explanation: In Wernicke's dysphasia, the primary deficit is in the comprehension of spoken speech; speech is faulty but fluent and produced without effort.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of Broca's dysphasia?

options.text: It is also known as receptive dysphasia
Writing is not affected
Normal rhythm and inflection are preserved
The patient is clearly under stress while trying to speak
The patient cannot usually recognize his or her mistakes

correct_answer.text: The patient is clearly under stress while trying to speak

correct_answers.text: The patient is clearly under stress while trying to speak

questions.explanation: Broca's dysphasia is expressive dysphasia; writing is affected in parallel with speaking, and comprehension is relatively intact. Speech is characteristically sparse, slow and hesitant, with marked disturbances of rhythm, inflexion and articulation. Wrong words are often chosen and marked reiteration and perseveration are common. The patient usually recognizes his or her mistakes and attempts to correct them.

questions.question_text: Regarding intelligence tests, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Alfred Binet introduced the concept of mental age
The Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS) comprises 11 subtests made up of six verbal subtests and five performance subtests
On the WAIS, the simplest level of brain damage may be reflected in discrepancies between the verbal and performance IQs
The performance subtests in the WAIS include digit span
Visuoperception, somatoperception and manual dexterity are tested in object assembly tests in performance subtests of the WAIS

correct_answer.text: The performance subtests in the WAIS include digit span

correct_answers.text: The performance subtests in the WAIS include digit span

questions.explanation: The visual subtests in the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale include digit span.

questions.question_text: Regarding the National Adult Reading Test, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: It is suitable for estimating premorbid intelligence
It may also be used to estimate premorbid levels of verbal fluency
In patients with dementia of moderate severity, it may yield an underestimate of premorbid competence
It is more suitable for estimating premorbid intelligence than the Schonell test
It is a culture-free test

correct_answer.text: It is a culture-free test

correct_answers.text: It is a culture-free test

questions.explanation: The level of word reading ability achieved by an adult has been shown to correlate highly with intelligence and, being well practised and overlearned, it proves to be relatively resistant to influences that impair other aspects of cognitive function. The National Adult Reading Test (NART) uses irregularly spelled words, which do not conform to rules (e.g. 'ache', 'bouquet', 'naive', etc.), and depends on correct pronunciation and strong familiarity. It is highly culture bound and is mainly used for patients with English as their first language.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is used as a rapid device for estimating performance IQ?

options.text: Raven's Progressive Matrices
The Bender-Gestalt Test
The Visual Object and Space Perception Battery
The Behavioural Inattention Test
The Token Test

correct_answer.text: Raven's Progressive Matrices

correct_answers.text: Raven's Progressive Matrices

questions.explanation: Raven's Progressive Matrices are used in clinical practice as a rapid device for estimating performance IQ. Usually the Mill Hill Vocabulary Test is also used to rapidly estimate verbal ability. The Bender-Gestalt Test is a rapid screening test of perception used to detect brain damage. The Visual Object and Space Perception Battery is another test for visual perception. The Behavioural Inattention Test is designed to examine unilateral visual neglect. The Token Test is sensitive to a minor degree of impairment of language comprehension.

questions.question_text: Regarding memory tests, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The Kendrick Object Learning Test is very stressful and less acceptable to elderly patients
Performance on the Benton Visual Retention Test correlates highly with intelligence and chronological age
Patients with dominant temporal lobe damage show major impairment with the Rey–Osterrieth Test
On the revised version of the Wechsler Memory Scale, practice effects can be avoided if testing is repeated
A shortened version of the Rivermead Behavioural Memory Test, used with aphasic patients, has been shown to be sensitive to the effects of language impairment rather than memory deficits

correct_answer.text: Performance on the Benton Visual Retention Test correlates highly with intelligence and chronological age

correct_answers.text: Performance on the Benton Visual Retention Test correlates highly with intelligence and chronological age

questions.explanation: The Kendrick Object Learning Test is less stressful and more acceptable to elderly patients, and is used in the assessment of dementia. Patients with dominant temporal lobe damage show little impairment with the Ray–Osterrieth Test, which involves copying a complex geometrical design. On the revised version of the Wechsler Memory Scale, practice effects cannot be avoided if testing is repeated, because the revision is presented in only one form. The shortened version of the Rivermead Behavioural Memory Test, used with aphasic patients, has been shown to be sensitive to the effects of memory deficits rather than language impairment.

questions.question_text: All of the following tests are good indicators of frontal lobe function, except:

options.text: Tests of Verbal Fluency
Wisconsin Card Sorting Test
Stroop Test
Mini Mental State Examination
Cognitive Estimates Test

correct_answer.text: Mini Mental State Examination

correct_answers.text: Mini Mental State Examination

questions.explanation: Tests of verbal fluency include the FAS Test. Patients with a left-sided frontal defect perform particularly badly on the Stroop Test.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of the Halstead–Reitan Battery?

options.text: It can indicate whether brain damage is focal or diffuse
It contains a category test
It includes detailed assessments of the accuracy of sensory perception on each side of the body
It tests finger recognition, graphaesthesia and stereognosis
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The Halstead–Reitan Battery also helps to determine whether the brain injury is located in the right or left hemisphere. It includes the Critical Flicker Frequency Test, the Tactual Performance Test, the Rhythm Test, the Speech Sound Perception Test, the Finger Tapping Test, the Time Sense Test, the Halstead–Wepman Aphasia Screening Test, and the Trait Making Test.

questions.question_text: Regarding dementia assessment, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: The Blessed Dementia Scale is administered to the patient
The Mini Mental State Examination is shown to discriminate well between patients with dementia and delirium
The Geriatric Mental State Schedule covers the period of a month prior to examination
The CAMCOG is specifically engineered to be user friendly for non-psychologists
DEMQOL is a computer program derived from the Geriatric Mental State Schedule that arrives at levels of confidence for diagnosing organic brain syndrome, schizophrenia, depression, etc.

correct_answer.text: DEMQOL is a computer program derived from the Geriatric Mental State Schedule that arrives at levels of confidence for diagnosing organic brain syndrome, schizophrenia, depression, etc.

correct_answers.text: DEMQOL is a computer program derived from the Geriatric Mental State Schedule that arrives at levels of confidence for diagnosing organic brain syndrome, schizophrenia, depression, etc.

questions.explanation: DEMQOL is a new measure to assess health-related quality of life in people with dementia. It is a 28-item interviewer-administered questionnaire answered by the person with dementia. AGECAT is a computer program derived from the Geriatric Mental State Examination, which arrives at levels of confidence for diagnosing organic brain syndrome, schizophrenia, depression, etc.

questions.question_text: Regarding objective measures of personality in adults, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI) does not emphasize major psychopathology
The 16 Personality Factor Questionnaire has limited usefulness with clinical populations
The Personality Assessment Inventory (PAI) does not include measures of psychopathology
The California Personality Inventory (CPI) is well accepted as a diagnostic tool in a clinical population
The Eysenck Personality Questionnaire (EPQ) is regarded as a very useful clinical diagnostic tool

correct_answer.text: The 16 Personality Factor Questionnaire has limited usefulness with clinical populations

correct_answers.text: The 16 Personality Factor Questionnaire has limited usefulness with clinical populations

questions.explanation: The Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory emphasizes major psychopathology. The 16 Personality Factor Questionnaire is used in research in the non-clinical population. The Personality Assessment Inventory includes measures of psychopathology, personality dimensions, validity scales, and specific concerns to psychotherapy treatments. The Eysenck Personality Questionnaire is useful only as a screening device.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scales is useful in establishing the severity of illness and monitoring the treatment response?

options.text: The Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression
The Hamilton Anxiety Scale
The Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale
The Structural Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Dissociative Disorders (SCID-D)
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Although used clinically, the greatest use for these scales is as research instruments; they help to standardize a subject cohort and provide objective outcome measures for assessing treatment response.

questions.question_text: The Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI) validity scale contains:

options.text: A lie scale
An infrequency scale
A suppressor scale
All of the above
None of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Response sets are attitudes or styles in responding to personality questionnaires. Some people answer incorrectly to present themselves in a more favourable light to please the examiner. Others attempt to look worse than they truly are. Well-designed tests like the Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory have built-in scales designed to detect such response sets and to adjust scores accordingly.

questions.question_text: The Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI) clinical scales include all of the following, except:

options.text: A depression scale
A phobia scale
A masculinity–femininity scale
A hysteria scale
A social introversion scale

correct_answer.text: A phobia scale

correct_answers.text: A phobia scale

questions.explanation: Other clinical scales include the Hypochondriasis Scale, the Psychopathic Deviance Scale, the Paranoia Scale, the Psychasthenia Scale, the Schizophrenia Scale, and the Hypomania Scale.

questions.question_text: Regarding projective measures of personality, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The Rorschach T est is the most widely used and best-researched projective device
There is no generally accepted scoring system for the Thematic Apperception T est and it is time consuming
The Sentence Completion T est is lengthy in administration time, and not useful in clinical interviews
In the Holtzman Inkblot T echnique, only one response is allowed per card
The Make-a-Picture-Story T est provides idiographic personality information through thematic analysis

correct_answer.text: The Sentence Completion T est is lengthy in administration time, and not useful in clinical interviews

correct_answers.text: The Sentence Completion T est is lengthy in administration time, and not useful in clinical interviews

questions.explanation: The Sentence Completion T est is brief in administration time, and can be useful in clinical interviews as an adjunct, if supplied beforehand.

questions.question_text: All neuropsychological deficits are associated mainly with left hemisphere damage, except:

options.text: Aphasia
Right–left disorientation
Finger agnosia
Anosognosia
Limb apraxia

correct_answer.text: Anosognosia

correct_answers.text: Anosognosia

questions.explanation: In anosognosia there is a lack of awareness of disease, particularly of hemiplegia, most often following a right parietal lesion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of the Luria–Nebraska Neuropsychological Battery?

options.text: A children's version is available for use with 8- to 12-year-olds
The test is extremely sensitive in identifying problems like dyslexia and dyscalculia
It helps to localize the various cortical zones that are involved in a particular function
It is useful in establishing left or right cerebral dominance
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The Luria–Nebraska Neuropsychological Battery assess a wide range of cognitive functions, including memory, motor functions, tactile, auditory and visual functions, speech, and writing.

questions.question_text: Regarding attitudes, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: A semantic differential scale is used to measure attitude
A five-point Likert scale is more sensitive in measuring attitudes than the dichotomous Thurstone Scale
The scapegoat theory of prejudice explains an ego-defensive function in which the person blames the outgroup for personal and social problems
In general, attitudes tend to predict behaviour if the individual is not aware of his or her attitudes
When a person's behaviours are inconsistent with his or her attitudes, cognitive dissonance leads the person to change these attitudes

correct_answer.text: In general, attitudes tend to predict behaviour if the individual is not aware of his or her attitudes

correct_answers.text: In general, attitudes tend to predict behaviour if the individual is not aware of his or her attitudes

questions.explanation: Attitudes tend to predict behaviour best when they are (1) strong and consistent; (2) specifically related to the behaviour being predicted; (3) based on a person's direct experience; and (4) when the person is aware of his or her attitudes.

questions.question_text: All of the following are objective tests of personality, except:

options.text: The Myers–Briggs Inventory
The Eysenck Personality Questionnaire
The Hostility and Direction of Hostility Questionnaire
The Q-Sort T est
The Sentence Completion T est

correct_answer.text: The Sentence Completion T est

correct_answers.text: The Sentence Completion T est

questions.explanation: The Sentence Completion T est is a subjective (projective) test. Other projective tests include the Rorschach T est, the Thematic Apperception T est, the Draw-a-Person T est and the Children's Apperception T est.

questions.question_text: Gardner's seven intelligences include all of the following, except:

options.text: Linguistic intelligence
Procedural intelligence
Musical intelligence
Bodily–kinaesthetic intelligence
Intrapersonal intelligence

correct_answer.text: Procedural intelligence

correct_answers.text: Procedural intelligence

questions.explanation: The other three are logical-mathematical intelligence, spatial intelligence and interpersonal intelligence.

questions.question_text: Regarding theories of intelligence, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Gardner's theory explains that the wide variety of adult roles found in different cultures cannot be explained by a single underlying intelligence
Anderson's theory explains the existence of a basic processing mechanism and specific processors for propositional thought and visual and spatial functioning
According to Sternberg's theory, differences in experience affect the ability to solve a given problem
Ceci's bioecological theory rejects the idea of single general capacity for abstract problem solving
According to Spearman's theory, factor sis the major determinant of performance on intelligence tests

correct_answer.text: According to Spearman's theory, factor sis the major determinant of performance on intelligence tests

correct_answers.text: According to Spearman's theory, factor sis the major determinant of performance on intelligence tests

questions.explanation: The originator of factor analysis, Spearman (1904), proposed that individuals possess a general intelligence factor (g) and special factors (s) specific to particular abilities or tests. According to Spearman, factor gis the major determinant of performance on intelligence tests.

questions.question_text: Regarding errors of assessment, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The Hawthorne effect occurs when the presence of an interviewer influences the response
The halo effect describes selecting answers to fit with other responses
Response set is a tendency always to agree or disagree with questions
Leniency error is a tendency to select extreme responses
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Social acceptability error describes the tendency to give answers expected by the interviewer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of IQ?

options.text: It is the ratio of mental age to chronological age
It has a normal distribution with a mean of 120 and a standard deviation of 15
There is a natural increase in intellectual ability with age
Performance IQ falls off with age more quickly than verbal IQ
Neither Stanford–Binet nor Wechsler scales are useful as predictors of achievement in school

correct_answer.text: Performance IQ falls off with age more quickly than verbal IQ

correct_answers.text: Performance IQ falls off with age more quickly than verbal IQ

questions.explanation: IQ is the ratio of mental age to chronological age/C2100; it has a normal distribution, with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15. Measured intelligence increases up to 16 years of age and plateaus until 25, after which it declines. Both the Stanford–Binet and the Wechsler scales are fair valid predictors of achievement in school.

questions.question_text: Regarding the validity of a test, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Predictive validity determines the extent of agreement between a present measurement and one in the future
Concurrent validity compares the measure being assessed with an external valid yardstick at the same time
Incremental validity refers to predictive validity and concurrent validity together
Divergent validity is established when measures discriminate successfully between other measures of unrelated constructs
Construct validity is determined by establishing both convergent and divergent validity

correct_answer.text: Incremental validity refers to predictive validity and concurrent validity together

correct_answers.text: Incremental validity refers to predictive validity and concurrent validity together

questions.explanation: Criterion validity refers to predictive validity and concurrent validity together. Incremental validity indicates whether the measurement being assessed is superior to other measurements in approaching true validity.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about the Present State Examination are true, except:

options.text: It is available in at least 35 languages, and has been widely used in many countries
It is a structured interview retaining the features of a clinical examination
It identifies abnormal phenomena that have been present during a defined period of time
It rates the severity of abnormal phenomena identified
It is not very useful in research, especially for the assessment of severe mental illness

correct_answer.text: It is not very useful in research, especially for the assessment of severe mental illness

correct_answers.text: It is not very useful in research, especially for the assessment of severe mental illness

questions.explanation: The Present State Examination is one of the most reliable means of assessment of severe mental illness available for research.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about the Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry (SCAN)?

options.text: They can be used to diagnose eating, somatoform, substance abuse and cognitive disorders
They have four possible ratings
They are compatible with PSE-9
They allow ICD-10 and DSM-IV diagnoses
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry also allow DSM-IIIR diagnoses; a computer-assisted version is available.

questions.question_text: The International Personality Disorder Examination (IPDE):

options.text: Does not assess phenomenology and life experiences
Is an instrument comprising 153 closed questions
Includes questions to determine frequency and duration
Does not try to establish age of onset
Establishes psychiatric diagnosis according to DSM-IV

correct_answer.text: Includes questions to determine frequency and duration

correct_answers.text: Includes questions to determine frequency and duration

questions.explanation: The International Personality Disorder Examination assesses phenomenology and life experiences, to enable psychiatric diagnosis according to ICD-10 and DSM-IIIR.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about standardized assessment tools are true, except:

options.text: The Diagnostic Interview Schedule (DIS) was used in the Epidemio-logical Catchment Area (ECA) project
The Structured Clinical Interview Schedule (SCID) is available as a patient edition for use in the clinical population and as a non-patient edition for use in epidemiological studies
The Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI) provides ICD-10 and DSM-IV diagnoses
In Diagnostic Interview Schedule (DIS), disorders occurring at any time in a person's life are taken into account
CATEGO is a computer program based on SCID

correct_answer.text: In Diagnostic Interview Schedule (DIS), disorders occurring at any time in a person's life are taken into account

correct_answers.text: In Diagnostic Interview Schedule (DIS), disorders occurring at any time in a person's life are taken into account

questions.explanation: CATEGO is a computer program based on the Present State Examination (PSE) that gives a symptom score and a diagnosis.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about instruments for measuring symptoms, except:

options.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAS) is designed for rating anxiety in other disorders
The Clinical Anxiety Scale is developed from the HAS, but focuses more on the symptoms of anxiety by leaving out depressive and somatic symptoms
The Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD) measures the severity of the depressive syndrome rather than the symptoms of depression
The Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) is usually completed by the patient
On the Montgomery–A ˚sberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS), only psychological symptoms of depression are rated by an interviewer

correct_answer.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAS) is designed for rating anxiety in other disorders

correct_answers.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAS) is designed for rating anxiety in other disorders

questions.explanation: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAS) was designed to be employed solely with anxiety disorders and not for rating anxiety in patients with other disorders.

questions.question_text: The Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) rates:

options.text: Blunted affect
Emotional withdrawal
Poor rapport
Difficulty in abstract and stereotyped thinking
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: PANSS also rates social withdrawal and lack of spontaneity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of the General Health Questionnaire?

options.text: It is designed as a screening instrument in primary care
The full version can be completed in 10 minutes
The full version contains 60 questions
The total score indicates overall severity, expressed as whether a psychiatrist would judge the patient as a 'case' or a 'non-case'
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: There is also a version with symptom subscales for somatic symptoms, anxiety and insomnia, depression and social dysfunction.

questions.question_text: A 58-year-old man with frontal lobe dementia starts to scribble on your table using your pen that was lying on it; when distracted from that he takes your spectacles from the table and puts them on. This behaviour is described as:

options.text: Wartenberg's reflex
Witzelsucht
Utilization behaviour
Perseveration
Magnetic syndrome

correct_answer.text: Utilization behaviour

correct_answers.text: Utilization behaviour

questions.explanation: Utilization behaviour is performance of a particular action beyond its relevance.

questions.question_text: A 64-year-old man with a history of left-sided parieto-occipital infarct can appreciate details of individual components of a complex picture but fails to understand the overall meaning of the picture. This phenomenon is known as:

options.text: Visual object agnosia
Prosopagnosia
Simultanagnosia
Anosognosia
Gerstmann's syndrome

correct_answer.text: Simultanagnosia

correct_answers.text: Simultanagnosia

questions.explanation: In simultanagnosia there is usually no difficulty in forming other meaningful concepts, since auditory information is quickly understood.

questions.question_text: A 68-year-old man with previous left-sided cerebral infarct is unable to point to or name any of his body parts when asked. This condition is known as:

options.text: Prosopagnosia
Hemiasomatognosia
Autotopagnosia
Microsomatognosia
Autoscopy

correct_answer.text: Autotopagnosia

correct_answers.text: Autotopagnosia

questions.explanation: In autotopagnosia, the patient exhibits an inability to point to or name body parts.

questions.question_text: A patient with early dementia is unable to carry out the coordinated sequences of actions when he is asked to take a match from a box and light it by striking. This is an example of:

options.text: Limb-kinetic apraxia
Ideomotor apraxia
Ideational apraxia
Constructional apraxia
Utilization behaviour

correct_answer.text: Ideational apraxia

correct_answers.text: Ideational apraxia

questions.explanation: In ideational apraxia, the patient is unable to carry out coordinated sequences of actions, but is able to copy simple actions.

questions.question_text: The Cambridge Examination for Mental Disorders of the Elderly (CAMDEX) incorporates:

options.text: The Mini Mental State Examination
The Blessed Dementia Rating Scale
The Hachinski Ischaemic Score
CAMCOG
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The Blessed Dementia Rating Scale is a measure of activities of daily living. The Hachinski Ischaemic Score helps differentiate between Alzheimer's dementia and vascular dementia. CAMCOG is the cognitive subscale of the CAMDEX.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of the Mini Mental State Examination?

options.text: It covers the basic cognitive functions
It is a diagnostic tool for vascular dementia
It measures registration recall and long-term memory
On the three-step paper-folding task, the patient should be prompted at each step if he or she is unable to register it
The language part of the test covers a wide variety of frontal lobe functions

correct_answer.text: It covers the basic cognitive functions

correct_answers.text: It covers the basic cognitive functions

questions.explanation: The Mini Mental State Examination is used only as a screening tool in dementia assessment; it measures registration recall, but not long-term memory; the three-step paper-folding task should not be prompted at each step.

questions.question_text: Regarding memory, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Verbal short-term memory is stored in the left hemisphere
Visual short-term memory is stored in the right hemisphere
During encoding, the left side of the brain is activated
During retrieval, the right side of the brain is activated
Visuomotor knowledge is an aspect of the organization of short-term memory

correct_answer.text: Visuomotor knowledge is an aspect of the organization of short-term memory

correct_answers.text: Visuomotor knowledge is an aspect of the organization of short-term memory

questions.explanation: Visuomotor knowledge and motor skills are aspects of the organization of long-term memory.

questions.question_text: Regarding memory, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: The visual association cortex is the anatomical correlate of iconic memory
The auditory association cortex is the anatomical correlate of echoic memory
The dominant parietal lobe is the anatomical correlate of auditory verbal short-term memory
The non-dominant temporo-occipital area is the anatomical correlate of visual verbal short-term memory
The non-dominant temporal lobe is the anatomical correlate of non-verbal short-term memory

correct_answer.text: The non-dominant temporo-occipital area is the anatomical correlate of visual verbal short-term memory

correct_answers.text: The non-dominant temporo-occipital area is the anatomical correlate of visual verbal short-term memory

questions.explanation: The dominant temporo-occipital area is the anatomical correlate of visual verbal short-term memory.

questions.question_text: Damage to which of the following brain structures results in an inability to store new memory?

options.text: Medial temporal lobes and hippocampus
Entorhinal cortex
Subiculum
Parahippocampal cortex
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Explicit memory involves all these structures. Memory probably passes from medial temporal lobe structures after a few weeks or months to longer-term storage in the cortex.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about implicit memory are true, except:

options.text: It is recalled automatically without effort
It is learnt slowly through repetition
It is readily amenable to verbal reporting
Its storage requires functioning of the cerebellum
Classical and operant learning involve implicit memory

correct_answer.text: It is readily amenable to verbal reporting

correct_answers.text: It is readily amenable to verbal reporting

questions.explanation: Implicit memory is not readily amenable to verbal reporting; storage requires functioning of the cerebellum and amygdala.

questions.question_text: Regarding the language areas of the brain, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Broca's area is involved in coordinating the organs of speech to produce coherent sounds
In lesions confined to Broca's area, the muscles involved in speech production are affected
Wernicke's area is involved in making sense of speech and language
Lesions of the angular gyrus produce an inability to read or write
Damage to the arcuate fasciculus results in a conduction dysphasia

correct_answer.text: In lesions confined to Broca's area, the muscles involved in speech production are affected

correct_answers.text: In lesions confined to Broca's area, the muscles involved in speech production are affected

questions.explanation: In lesions confined to Broca's area, the muscles involved in speech production work normally.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about agnosia is true?

options.text: Agnosia may result from impairment in the sensory pathways
Frontal lobe lesions usually cause pseudoagnosia
Lesions in the right occipital lobe result in apperceptive agnosia
Lesions in the left parieto-occipital areas result in associative agnosia
Astereognosia is the inability to recognize numbers or letters traced on the palm

correct_answer.text: Lesions in the left parieto-occipital areas result in associative agnosia

correct_answers.text: Lesions in the left parieto-occipital areas result in associative agnosia

questions.explanation: Agnosia is the inability to interpret and recognize the significance of sensory information that does not result from impairment in the sensory pathways.

questions.question_text: Frontal lobe lesions can cause:

options.text: Pallilalia
Echolalia
Logoclonia
Motor Jacksonian fits
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Reiteration of phrases just spoken (echolalia), of single words (pallilalia) or a terminal syllable (logoclonia) are perseverative errors of speech occurring in frontal lobe damage.
